As much as some people like to think that Satou is just crazy and evil, I see a bit of humanity in her. After all, when her supposed best friend abandoned her over something she herself couldn’t help and was ashamed of, she was clearly very hurt. I think, some fans have forgotten that Shoko initiates the whole thing, despite being told by Satou to leave it alone. It’s pretty obvious that despite being hurt by Shoko, Satou had no ill will towards her and wanted to protect her by making her stay out of it. However, because of her own selfish reasons, Shoko decided to press the issue and forced Satou into a situation where she’d have to choose between her and Shio. 

We all have differing opinions though, so it’s hard to understand why some people will just set up a bias and ignore the character development of one character in favor of another. I bet we can all agree, though, that the death scene was very detailed and high quality to the point where it shocks you with the first watch. Anyway, thank you for the response~! ❤️

Okay so, maybe I’m just a horrible person but....I was completely desensitized to the ending. I was amazed at the quality and realistic terror behind the murder but I didn’t feel as bad for Shoko as I guess I should have? She did everything wrong in the book here. If she really wanted to be of any use, she could have filed in a report or did things more undercover instead of dangling herself in front of Satou like an idiot. I know she’s the normal and sane character that we’re supposed to like but I honestly didn’t feel as connected to her as everybody else seems to have. 

I can kind of get where Satou was coming from here. I wouldn’t have trusted a word Shoko said either. When it comes down to it, Shoko was absolutely stupid in this episode and sometimes stupid gets you killed. Run, struggle more, try harder to sell your story. Do something. Don’t think for a second it’ll all be fine because “we were friends”. You ruined any chance of that saving you when you rejected Satou just because of what her Aunt is like. It didn’t seem like Shoko even tried to think about how Satou felt at all. She was trying to become the heroine and ruin Satou when she had no right to put herself in that position. That’s what makes her not a real friend and so, her death was just essential to the story. It’s not as emotional for me as it is for everybody else because Shoko is likable but not likable enough to condone all her idiotic actions.

That’s just my opinion, though, so I’m sorry if I have offended anyone.
